messages:
alex: Quick sync — we need to finalize the archival SLA and forensics playbook for Q3 roadmap. Primary ask: define evidence retention windows + export latency for incident investigations. @meera @jamie any blockers?
meera: Need clarity on two things: 1) per-tenant vs org-level retention, 2) whether HSM-backed keys are required for archived evidence. Both affect cost and SOC2 scope.
jamie: +1. Also, what counts as "evidence" for exports? full request/response logs, debug traces, and KV cache snapshots? We should be explicit.
kevin: From legal: preservation order = immediate hold; export SLA must be <= 24h for high-priority holds. For standard requests legal is ok with 7 days.
anna: Product input: customers want self-service exports in console for standard cases. For holds we need an approval flow. That impacts launch criteria.
sre-bot: deploy: archival-policy-v2.md has been pushed to /docs/retention (link: https://internal.redwood/docs/retention/archival-policy-v2).
meera: Good. Proposal: baseline retention 90d for request logs, 365d for audit logs, 7y for legal-critical artifacts. HSM required for 7y tier only. Thoughts?
alex: That seems reasonable as a starting point. We need explicit rollout gating: 1) KMS/HSM integration tests green, 2) export encryption-at-rest verified, 3) UI approval workflow implemented.
jamie: Can we define the export latency SLO matrix? Suggest: immediate retrieval for self-service (<1m), queued export for legal holds (<24h), cold-archive retrieval (if applicable) <72h.
kevin: Legal happy with that if chain-of-custody metadata is preserved (user id, timestamp, export hash). Add WORM flag to the 7y tier.
meera: Technical constraints: current object store lifecycle transitions to glacier-like tiers will add 24-72h delay. That means cold-archive retrieval SLO must be explicit. Also HSM key rotation flow must not break access to older archives — need exportable key-wrapping policy.
anna: Launch criteria suggestion: must support per-tenant holds, admin approval workflow, chain-of-custody metadata, HSM protected keys for long-term tier, and a dry-run export mode for customers. If dry-run fails we block.
alex: Prioritization: MVP (Q3): per-tenant holds, UI approval, standard export (<7d), chain-of-custody. Phase 2 (Q4): HSM long-term tier, cold-archive retrieval SLA, self-service for >365d.
jamie: Dev note: will need a migration plan for existing archives to mark retention tiers and attach KMS key ids. I'll open a ticket with migration steps.
meera: Ops note: for forensics we need immutable export logs and signed hashes. I'll draft schema for export manifest: `{
  "export_id": "string",
  "initiator": "string",
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "objects": [ "s3://..." ],
  "hash": "sha256",
  "timestamp": "iso"
}`

alex: Perfect. Can you post that schema to the doc and tag legal + compliance?
meera: Posted and tagged @kevin @anna. Link in doc.
kevin: approve: legal sign-off on proposed retention tiers and SLOs pending final wording in runbook.
anna: Product OK to ship MVP if migration and approval flow scoped to a single region first.
alex: Next actions: 1) meera to PR HSM integration tests, 2) jamie to create migration ticket, 3) anna to scope UI approval flows, 4) kevin to finalize legal wording. We'll reconvene Friday. :thumbsup:
kevin: noted.
meera: I'll aim to have tests by Thu.
jamie: migration ticket created: TKT-4321.
anna: I'll post a short spec doc by EOD tomorrow.
alex: Thanks all — closing thread for now.
